<!-- pr-reviewer: 5d47d22d1916076c45b645c20ac9c0d875a14b43 -->
**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.**

Review tier: standard. The change is to the refusal text only. It does not change motion, posted G-code, gouge checks, stock simulation or geometry. I did two mutations to make sure that the new pins work.

### What looks good
- The fix is small and in the correct location (`crates/motion/src/machining3d/ladder.rs`). The flag `too_narrow` is set only when the level target is not empty and the eroded cutter-centre area is empty. Thus the filled-model text stays for a model that fills all levels.
- `pocket3d` and `pocket3d_offset` both use the ladder. The new test file pins all three texts for both entry points.
- The callers match `GenError::Empty(_)` by variant, not by text (`run_rest`, and the masked branch in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`). The new text does not change their behaviour.
- No added `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!` in production code. `ladder.rs` has 371 lines. The test file has a provenance line and a gate map.
- The decision file `docs/decisions/1709-pocket-refusal.md` is in the correct format. The body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1709`. There are no changes to goldens, snapshot PNGs, `PROCESS_VERSION`, dependencies, `.github/` or `scripts/`. There are no `crates/ui` changes, thus no screenshots are necessary.

### Results (local, merged with main `14aa3abd`)
The trial merge with `upstream/main` was clean.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --no-fail-fast` (84 test targets: lib, bin, all integration tests, doc-tests) | 956 passed, 0 failed, 52 ignored |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test pocket_refusal` | 3 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test remachining` | 6 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test probe_only_sim` | 2 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test shared_face_bodies` | **4 passed, 1 failed**, 1 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

The failure:

```
---- the_sample_as_imported_refuses_the_3d_pocket_by_name stdout ----
panicked at crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies.rs:177:5:
{"content":[{"text":"generate: R1 - could not generate the toolpath: R1: nothing to machine: nothing to cut: the open area is too narrow for the 6 mm tool and 0 mm stock to leave at every level","type":"text"}],"isError":true}
```

### Mutations (local)
1. I removed `too_narrow = true;`. Result: `narrow_pocket_names_the_tool` and `stock_allowance_names_the_clearance_needed` failed. `filled_pocket_names_the_model` passed. With this mutation, `the_sample_as_imported_refuses_the_3d_pocket_by_name` passed. Thus the failure above comes from this PR, not from main.
2. I changed the condition to `if too_narrow || true`. Result: `filled_pocket_names_the_model` failed, and `machining3d::degenerate_input_refuses_cleanly` also failed (it reads "fills").

I restored the code after each mutation. The tree was identical to the PR head after the restore.

### Requested before merge
1. `crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies.rs:177` - This test is the #1706 sample (`sample_ap214.step` as imported, EM-0600-4FL). It pins the old text, thus it fails now. Change the expected text to `nothing to cut: the open area is too narrow for the 6 mm tool and 0 mm stock to leave at every level`. Also update the doc comment at lines 164-170, which tells that the old text is correct. This test is the end-to-end proof of #1709. The PR body tells "The STEP sample from #1706 was not imported", but this test imports it and shows that the fix gives the correct text. The gate quick run did not select the suite because its gate map (line 8-10) names only `camcraft_motion::machining3d::rest`. Please also add `camcraft_motion::machining3d` (or `machining3d::ladder`) to that gate map, so that the gate selects this test for a ladder change in the future.

### Notes (not blocking)
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/ladder.rs:358` - The format is `{}` for the diameter and the stock to leave. A diameter that comes from an inch conversion can show many decimals (for example `2.5400000000000005`). Other refusals in the crate use `{:.3}` (`adaptive_troch.rs:82`, `trochoid_slot.rs:159`). `rest2d.rs:205` uses `{}`. Thus both forms are in the crate. You can use `{:.3}` or a trimmed format. This is your decision.
- The text says "at every level". If some top levels are filled by the model and the lower levels are too narrow, then "at every level" is not fully correct. The cause that the user must correct (the tool) is correct. Thus this is only a wording note.
- `site/content/guide/operations-3d.md:65` lists the old refusal in "Common refusals". You can add the new text there in a follow-up.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
